past month I've kept a journal where I put an 'X' next to every date where a GitHub outage has negatively impacted my ability to work... Almost every day has an X
It really has been remarkable watching GitHub just crumble as an organization... The unofficial status page tells a horrifying story.
The writing was already on the wall when MS required logins to search code just 48 hours after acquisition
Between this and my company's proxy screwing with HTTP/2 at least once a day the frustration is very very real. While I'm nowhere as invested in GitHub its decline does make me sad.
Tangentially related, but maybe microsoft could actually do that: why is github's search so terribly bad? ... it's simply more efficient to clone and use plain old grep, it's really sad.

Can you please prioritize stability of your SaaS offering for paying customers? Our dev team and infra gets impacted seemingly every week with github outages, and it especially seems to correlate with delivery of new features.
This is pretty cool... GitHub is now free for teams. Seems like Github is feeling heat from GitLab/BitBucket.
I've not been a big fan of GitHub historically, but the pace of innovation since the MS acquisition is really impressive.
One thing to note is I had 3 members, it did not automatically downgrade my seats from 5. So in order to get it down to $12 a month I had to go downgrade my seats from 5 to 3.

what sucks more is Github creating default main branch on repo creation. It's an unwarranted hassle to rename it and if you don't rename it, you will definitely try to push to master and then realize the mistake.
I switched from Github to Gitlab after this change [master/main rename].

I've been using the [Copilot] alpha for the past 2 weeks, and I'm blown away. Copilot guesses the exact code I want to write about one in ten times... when it guesses right, it feels like it's reading my mind.
It's funny that GitHub ships their own text editor, Atom, but the second example on the Copilot website is clearly using VSCode.
